companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Freddie Mac, shorthand for the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., jumped 11 spots on this year’s Fortune 500. The government-backed enterprise provides liquidity to the housing market through its purchase of home mortgages from small banks and credit unions, among other lenders. From there, Freddie Mac (like Fannie Mae) holds on to these mortgages or packages the loans into mortgage-backed securities that can be sold.

  • Freddie Mac raked in $86.7 billion in revenue in 2022, a nearly 32% increase from the previous year.

  • The company had a shaky start to 2023: In the first quarter, it reported revenue of $4.8 billion, down 17% year over year, and net income of $2 billion, which represents a 47% decline from 2021. Overall, its new business activity in the first quarter of 2023 was down 72% year over year, as higher mortgage rates slowed home sales and refinancing.

  • In 2022, Freddie Mac financed 1.8 million mortgages (with 58% of eligible loans affordable for low- and moderate-income families) and 693,000 rental units (with 96% of eligible units affordable for low- and moderate-income families).

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The government-backed mortgage provider had an eventful year as the U.S. housing market entered uncharted territory in 2021. Between a historically low inventory of homes for sale and soaring demand, Freddie Mac—which buys and securitizes mortgages issued by commercial lenders—was still able to help nearly 5 million families buy, refinance, or rent their homes in 2021, helping keep interest rates lower.

companyRankingLists.description: Total revenue for the world’s biggest companies fell 4.8% to $31.7 trillion this year—the first decline in half a decade.
companyRankingLists.title: Fortune Global 500
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Like its sister government-backed entity, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac played a major role in ensuring the U.S. housing market continued to function amid an unprecedented pandemic. The company provided approximately $1.2 trillion in liquidity to the mortgage market in 2020, in the process financing nearly 3.8 million single-family home loans—including 2.7 million refinancings that enabled homeowners to capitalize on record-low interest rates. While the pandemic contributed to a nearly 12% drop in Freddie’s revenues last year, profits remained resilient and climbed nearly 2% in 2020.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Like Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac is still government controlled. Also like Fannie, it saw a steep decline in profits last year, which were down 22%, even as the lender's top line grew more than 2%. The financials don’t tell the whole story, however. Freddie plays an outsized role in helping millions of Americans own or rent a home, providing nearly $558 billion in liquidity to the mortgage market last year. In 2019, it served nearly 95% of all single-family home lenders in the country—and it's seeing growth with younger families and couples. First-time home buyers represented nearly half of Freddie’s new single-family purchase loans last year.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
